OpenTune {{APP_VERSION}} with the local control API - unofficial test build {{BUILD_LABEL}}
INSTALL (macOS {{MIN_MACOS}} or later, Apple silicon only)

(中文：INSTALL.zh-CN.txt)

This is NOT an official OpenTune release. The only official channel is
{{OFFICIAL_RELEASES_URL}}. Read README-UNOFFICIAL.txt first.

The commands below are for the Terminal app. Replace <folder> with the folder
you extract the package to.


1. Install official OpenTune first
----------------------------------

- Install official OpenTune for macOS, version {{MIN_OFFICIAL_VERSION}} or later,
  from {{OFFICIAL_RELEASES_URL}}
  in the default location (/Applications/OpenTune.app).
- This package contains no model weights. This build uses the models of that
  installation (inside OpenTune.app, in Contents/Resources/models). Without
  them, pitch detection, note generation and rendering do not work.
- This build runs on Apple silicon Macs (M1 and later) with macOS {{MIN_MACOS}}
  or later. Intel Macs are not supported.


2. Check the download
---------------------

- Compare the SHA-256 of the zip with the value on the release page:

    shasum -a 256 ~/Downloads/{{PACKAGE_NAME}}.zip


3. Extract
----------

- Extract the zip to a folder of your own, for example ~/OpenTune-test
  (create it first). Double-clicking the zip in Finder works, or:

    mkdir -p <folder>
    ditto -x -k ~/Downloads/{{PACKAGE_NAME}}.zip <folder>

  Do not put OpenTune-ctl.app into the official OpenTune.app or replace the
  official OpenTune.app. The names differ, so both can sit side by side.
- Check every extracted file against SHA256SUMS (every line must say OK) and
  the signature of the app (no output means it is intact):

    cd <folder>/{{PACKAGE_NAME}}
    shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
    codesign --verify --deep --strict OpenTune-ctl.app


4. Allow the first start
------------------------

The app is signed ad hoc and not notarized by Apple, so macOS Gatekeeper
blocks the first start of OpenTune-AI.command and of OpenTune-ctl.app. If the
hashes in steps 2 and 3 matched, allow them in one of two ways:

- System Settings -> Privacy & Security: after the blocked start, scroll down
  to the message about the blocked item and click "Open Anyway" (macOS asks
  for your password). Do this for OpenTune-AI.command, and again for
  OpenTune-ctl.app when it is blocked.
- Or remove the quarantine mark of the whole folder in Terminal (the zip
  extraction marks every file when the zip came from a browser):

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <folder>/{{PACKAGE_NAME}}


5. Start
--------

- OpenTune-AI.command (double-click it in Finder; Terminal opens briefly)
  starts OpenTune-ctl.app with the local control API on. Use it when OpenTune
  MCP Server should operate OpenTune. Extra arguments given to the script are
  passed on to OpenTune. It changes no settings and writes no files.
- To let OpenTune MCP Server start OpenTune itself, set its environment
  variable OPENTUNE_MCP_OPENTUNE_PATH to the full path of OpenTune-AI.command
  in this folder. The server wants opentune-control.json next to the program it
  starts, and that file sits next to OpenTune-AI.command (it cannot be inside
  the app: the signature of the app would not hold).
- Opening OpenTune-ctl.app directly (double-click) starts OpenTune with the
  control API off.
- Quit official OpenTune before you start this build, and do not run both at
  the same time.


6. Settings and logs are shared with official OpenTune
------------------------------------------------------

- This build uses the same settings and log files as official OpenTune (in
  your user Library folder, ~/Library/OpenTune). Changes made in one appear in
  the other.
- While the control API is on, OpenTune writes a discovery file to
  ~/Library/Application Support/OpenTune/control/instances/ and deletes it on
  normal exit.


7. Uninstall
------------

- Quit OpenTune.
- Delete <folder>/{{PACKAGE_NAME}} (or the folder you extracted to).
- Delete ~/Library/Application Support/OpenTune/control/ (files of the control
  API).
- Do not delete ~/Library/OpenTune: official OpenTune uses it too.
